newsitem.title: FRANCE: No quick solutions to French jobless rate - Aubry.
newsitem.headline: No quick solutions to French jobless rate - Aubry.

text.p: French Employment Minister Martine Aubry told a news conference on Tuesday she was not counting on a marked improvement in jobs creation in the coming months.

"At the ministry I am told...current job creation trends do not allow us to count on a significant improvement in the coming months," she told her first news conference since taking over an enlarged employment ministry in the new left-wing government.
Aubry is considered as Prime Minister's "Number Two" in the government formed after a June 1 election when the centre-right was ousted from power.
Unemployment data released on Monday showed that the number of jobless leapt by 32,400 in May after several months of small declines.
"Given the current economic context I was surprised by the falls of the previous months. I was unfortunately not surprised by the rise (in May). But (about) 30,000 is enormous," she said.

Aubry said she would not resort to "artificial methods" such as "rigged statistics" to improve employment numbers and that work on the programme to create 350,000 public sector jobs would not be designed to created "little jobs" or the "fill the gaps".
